but what was great about cartridges? Memory management controllers. (or "memory bank controller" on gameboys)

basically, it was a chip in the cartridge that via some clever coding added additional hardware to the console, allowing "yoshi's island" to take place, being able to stretch, scale and so forth, the blob boss is a marvellous example of this. it's also why "starfox" was able to exist on the snes. it was also able to add 3 more sound channels(you can see people using the concept of it on the famitracker forums or reddit's /r/chiptunes (the VRC6 chip)). or even on the gameboy, add 4 new color palettes for characters/objects AND background tiles, or increasing the amount of colors per sprite or sprites per screen/big sprite by making rendering more efficient. it really gave devs the opportunity to press the console to its limits and really shape the experience after their vision

Looking for romance in a harem seems like a mistake. Most harems don't have a clear direction of which character(s) are going to be pursued since it's often the case that the source material hasn't been finished, MCs (main characters) are written as aloof/stupid/indecisive, arcs are written like a hellish never ending OVA where there's no real progression (Nisekoi), it could be poorly written, or intended as trashy masturbation material without any substance.

Another problem with anime in the romance genre is miscategorization. You often have it tacked on as a subgenre when it should be "simplified romance-like elements" or "cute girls and their cute reactions to situations." I think Infinite Stratos falls into this category while Oreimo had a more proper romance genre.

Romance is pretty niche, especially when looking at anime for the shounen demographic. It feels like there's more romance for shoujo (Princess Tutu, Ore Monogatari), josei (Princess Jellyfish, Nana, Usagi Drop), or seinen (Spice and Wolf, Oreimo, Arakawa Under the Bridge, Danna ga Nani). Remember it's a niche genre, read the source material for your favorites, lament it's a niche genre, and start reading more manga and light novels without anime adaptations.

Yes and we don't disagree. One of the key differences seems to be the difference between 'chronic' or what I called 'habitual' smokers. I mentioned it might just be 1 or 2 joints a day. Its not necessarily the amount. Someone else might smoke the 'bongloads' at various weekly college parties totally more drugs (overall average) BUT the habitual one may be the one who is really fucked on withdrawal when there is nothing for a week. 'Bong Load Champ' may not actually notice much after leaving college and going months forever without smoking up.

The best advice my doctor ever gave on drugs (as in drugs that get you high/low, painkillers etc) but he said you simply dont take them consistently and you'll avoid addiction.

Two of my family members are actually going through something much worse than their usual cranky attitudes when they'd go without weed for a few days. Its something where after 25+ years of consistent habitual weed smoking they started getting:

  • Sudden full-on paranoia attacks and 'bad trips' and these are guys who never had that for 3 decades of smoking.

  • even stranger - often getting almost zero effects. One was so frustrated he'd just do a gram (of strong stuff) for next-to-nothing while his regular smoke-up buddies were clearly stoned out of their minds on less from the same bags.

One started getting what was a bit misdiagnosed as 'Panic Attacks'. They were 'panic attacks' but he wasnt fitting the standard conditions and other symptoms and his were so strangely random and oddball. The doctor finally started looking into some major long-term marijuana studies in Italy and other European studies and it turns out this is a real phenom and it almost only happens to 30 year habitual pot smokers. Not 10 years. Not 15 or even 20 but actually happens to the 30 year markers and it includes 'mock panic attacks', mock 'immunity', random 'bad trip' experiences or even pseudo-epileptic seizures. Which he had started getting. Which were not really 'epileptic seizures' and finally one other system this relative did NOT get but the other one did which was..

Schizophrenia. Well again a kind of 'pseudo-schizophrenia' or he was classed as having developed 'schizo-affective disorder' or some spectrum of that. But basically Relative #2 caught on to the '30 year chronic' problems at about year 20. He quit for maybe 3 years and we remember him having a 'break down' about the stupid crazy thoughts and blaming it on the drugs, the pot. He did improve a LOT over 3 years. Like just being a normal dude, more rational, more responsible, his business started doing very well and then he started small habitual smoking again. Its sad really. He went from standard 'Ron Paul' and 'R-Conspiracy' nonense into the goverment surveilling his home to full-on shit about alien spaceships and how neighbours (as in anywhere) are hacking his phone and holy shit you name it. No, he does this NOT HIGH.

I should mention this relative never had any kind of mental issues for at least the first 40 years of his life and certainly nothing anything like 'schizo' issues. Was also a very down-to-earth type who was fairly skeptical and not prone to fantasy or 'UFO sightings' or that kind of thing.

The good news (so we're told by drug and psych people) is that this kind of 'schizophrenia' is actually well known to go away too. Its not true schizophrenia and can fade away even 6 months later until effectively 'gone' for any medical point of view. But yep. Is that from marijuana? Even he thought that was what was causing it. And this was before the latest studies now confirming some strong indications.

but back to the OP: yes I can agree that while a lot of marijuana smokers do totally fall into 'stoner sloth' it might be more of a decision made outside the weed (planning to do nothing all day then getting high to aid and facilitate that slothy plan) because yes actually many marijuana people, 'Oxy Addicts' and amazingly alcoholics are high-functioning and surprisingly productive!
